text:
Sam Malinski went undrafted out of Cornell and became, by Evolving-Hockey's measure, the eighth most valuable defenseman in the league last season, 3.1 wins above replacement, mostly from defense. This season the Avalanche are leaning on him more: over 20 minutes a night across his last ten games, and 23 or more in his last two.

He still doesn't have a goal. Zero on 30 shots and 1.4 expected goals, which is a small, fixable drought for a defenseman; our range on his shooting runs from 4% to 7%. The assists have covered for it, nine in 20 games and seven in his last ten.

There's luck in his line too, the other direction. Colorado has scored 10.8 more goals than expected with him on the ice, while its expected goals share with him is just about even. That gap usually closes. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 95th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists last season and the 91st for chances from in front of the net. Watch for the first goal, and watch whether the minutes stay up.
